turns.prompt_text: can you ride e-scooters in Minneapolis
turns.response_html: Yes, you can ride e-scooters in Minneapolis, but they are strictly prohibited on sidewalks; you must use bike lanes, paths, or the right-hand side of the road. While the city's shared scooter program—featuring providers like Lime and Spin—typically operates seasonally from April through November, you must be at least 12 years old to ride, and helmets are required for anyone under 18.

turns.prompt_text: can I ride my scooter on the sidewalk
turns.response_html:
No, you cannot ride on the sidewalk in Minneapolis.

State law and city ordinances require you to use bike lanes or the right-hand side of the road. You may only briefly use the sidewalk when entering or leaving a property.

Quick Rules:

  • Where to ride: Use bike paths, lanes, or streets with speed limits of 30 mph or less.
  • Speed limit: Maintain a maximum speed of 15 mph.
  • Age: You must be at least 12 years old.
  • Helmets: Required for riders under 18.
